h2: Water Leak Repair Sanur – Finding & Fixing Hidden Leaks
intro: If your PDAM meter keeps spinning or the pump won't stop, there's likely a hidden leak somewhere in the villa. Water Leak Repair Sanur covers everything from a drip under the kitchen sink to a burst pipe behind a bathroom wall — especially common in villas that are 15–20 years old. Snap a few photos and send them over WhatsApp; pricing depends on what we find.

sections.h3: Why Older Sanur Villas Leak More
sections.text: Villas built 15–20 years ago still run on original PVC pipework, and decades of sun exposure make those fittings brittle enough to crack without warning. In Sindhu and Semawang the salt-laden sea air accelerates corrosion on tap cartridges, pump motors and exposed joints, so even small drips escalate faster than inland. Add brackish well water near the coast and you get clogged filters plus scale buildup in heaters — all signs that something upstream is leaking into the system.

sections.h3: The Jobs We See Most Around Here
sections.text: A slow drip under the bathroom sink, a shower floor drain that never fully seals, or garden irrigation lines splitting where they run across gravel — these are the bread-and-butter calls. Burst PVC or PPR pipes behind walls show up as damp patches on plaster or a pump that runs non-stop. In Mertasari and Sanur Kauh, older villas often have both PDAM and well connections, which doubles the number of joints where a leak can start.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for a Quote
sections.text: A clear photo of the affected area — under the sink, around the shower base, or the garden line in question — plus a shot of your water meter if you suspect a hidden leak. Tell us roughly how long the drip has been going and whether the pump cycles constantly. Pricing depends entirely on what we find once we're on site, so there's no fixed rate; the quote comes after we've seen the photos and scoped the work.

sections.h3: Keeping Leaks at Bay in Sanur's Climate
sections.text: Check exposed pipe joints every few months, especially in Sindhu where salt air eats through fittings quickly. If your villa runs a well, flush the filter housing quarterly to stop brackish sediment from clogging valves. Replace any PVC section that looks chalky or sun-cracked rather than patching it — a fresh coupling holds far better in heat. And if you notice a musty smell near the septic tank, book a pump-out before grease and paper build up enough to back up into the bathroom.

faq.q: How do I tell if there's a hidden leak behind the wall?
faq.a: Turn off every tap and flush, then watch the PDAM meter for ten minutes. If the dial still moves or your pump keeps cycling, water is escaping somewhere you can't see.

faq.q: Do you cover all of Sanur, including Sindhu and Mertasari?
faq.a: Yes — we work across Sanur Kaja, Sanur Kauh, Sindhu, Semawang, Mertasari and Batujimbar. Just send photos over WhatsApp and we'll sort out the details from there.

faq.q: Is it better to replace a cracked PVC section or patch it?
faq.a: In most cases here, replacing the short run of pipe is smarter. Sun-brittle PVC doesn't hold a patch well in Bali's heat, so a new coupling and fitting lasts far longer.
